#4505. The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and HD Are the Right Amount of Too Much

Familiar designs with big changes underneath, including a new monstrous 8.3-liter turbodiesel in the HD.

Chevrolet decorated its event introducing the updated 2027 Silverado pickups with Chevy trucks from the past. The old trucks are gorgeous in their archaic way. But get up close and they’re all painted metal, rubber mats, and yawning panel gaps. Old trucks were expected to do one thing: work hard. New trucks are expected to do everything.

Chevrolet took Road & Track to Tucson, Arizona, to experience the both the “light duty” Silverado 1500 and the beefier Silverado HD. That’s “HD” as in Heavy Duty. The abilities of both of these full-size Silverados have vastly expanded, but the case for choosing between them has vastly narrowed. The new Silverado 1500 does things only the HD models once did, and the Silverado HD now rides nearly as well and is otherwise as comfortable as any lighter-duty truck has ever been. I found it hard to imagine a civilian duty cycle that would lie outside these trucks’ abilities. Or to imagine full-size trucks easier to live with every day.

The beating hearts of these revised trucks are new engines: new 5.7- and 6.6-liter small-block V-8s in the Silverado 1500 and a monstrously torque-rich turbodiesel V-8 that’s offered in the HD. At 8.3 liters, that diesel is the largest-displacement engine General Motors has ever sent into the consumer market.

Keep in mind that both the 1500 and the HD are offered with huge choice of configurations. The 1500, for instance, is available in five different cab and bed combinations and seven trim levels ranging from the WT work truck to the off-road beastmaster ZR2. There’s also, variously, rear- or four-wheel drive and four different engines, including an updated turbocharged 2.7-liter inline-four and a returning 3.0-liter turbodiesel inline-six. Every 2027 Silverado at the Arizona event, with one notable exception, was a well-equipped four-by-four. So, this is only a peek at a sliver of the high-end tippy-top of the Silverado line.

Let’s start with the Silverado 1500. The sheetmetal largely carries over, and the basic chassis design has only modestly evolved, but the new V-8s are sweet things indeed. Both the 5.7- and 6.6-liter displacements are familiar from small-block history. GM says these are sixth-generation engines, sharing their architecture with the 6.7-liter small-block in the 2027 Corvette Stingray and Grand Sport. It’s an evolutionary step, still a cam-in-block, overhead-valve, two-valve design. The increase in displacement is the result of a 6-mm increase in piston stroke.

The 5.7-liter displacement—350 cubic inches in old muscle terms—was the stalwart of GM’s truck-engine lineup from the 1969 model year through 1998, when the LS-series small-block arrived. The new 5.7 essentially replaces the 5.3-liter version and is rated by GM at 402 hp with 428 lb-ft of peak torque. That’s up 46 hp from the 2026 Silverado’s 5.3-liter.

The 5.7 operated effortlessly in an unladen Silverado 1500 running the now-familiar 10-speed automatic transmission. Thrust was ample, and the engine operated in near silence. The transmission has apparently had some behavior modification since I last drove one, with more positive and confident shifts. Previous 10-speeds have wandered between gears.

Properly configured, a 5.7 Silverado can be rated to tow up to 13,700 pounds. Airstream’s biggest trailer, filled with stuff, is around 10,000 pounds. That’s so much towing capacity that, frankly, it makes moving up to an HD unnecessary for most buyers. The 6.6-liter small-block is rated at 481 hp and 501 lb-ft of peak torque. It was best showcased in the ZR2, where it helped the nearly three-ton truck practically glide over semi-rough terrain and across rutted trails. During this initial exposure, it was vice-free and easygoing, which wasn’t unexpected.

In celebration of America’s continued commitment to imperial units of measurement, and in recognition of small-block heritage, GM has cast “350” into the 5.7-liter block and “400” into the 6.6. They’re virtually impossible to see once the engine is installed in a truck, but it’s so cool anyhow.

The inside of the 1500 is updated with bigger screens—a massive 16.3-incher at the center, a 12.2-inch unit in front of the driver, and an 11.5-inch screen to keep the front-seat passenger entertained. It worked well with Apple CarPlay integration and there were still enough buttons and physical controls to keep the photons from demanding constant attention. Off-road, the various cameras aboard will pump images to the center screen making spotters superfluous except in the most extreme circumstances. For someone who is usually a lukewarm Luddite on digital displays, their value and potential become obvious navigating tight trails.

Acclimating to and exploring the dazzling and dizzying array of drive modes on the ZR2 could eat up an entire three-year lease. It’s enough, however, to know that getting stuck will take some willful effort in this immensely capable truck.

On-road, higher-trim Silverado 1500s feature semi-autonomous SuperCruise driving. It’s at the point now where SuperCruise is so competent at lane holding and stability that it feels more secure with a trailer than I ever have.

But for all its superfluousness for most truck needers, there is something glorious about the Silverado HD. Especially the new diesel version. The Mongoose 8.3-liter turbodiesel V-8 is misnamed. It ought to just be “Mongo” after the horse-punching mountain of a man played by Alex Karras in Blazing Saddles. But unlike Mongo, this engine is not merely a pawn in the game of life.

In a Silverado HD 3500-series dualie optimized for maximum towing, with a trailer laden up to 37,000 pounds (max is 38,000 pounds), the Mongoose proved shockingly capable when I drove the whole configuration down a drag strip. That was 18.5 tons being pulled by a single pickup truck on a fifth wheel and gooseneck.

The Mongoose is an all-new engine built around a compacted graphite iron (CGI) block. NASCAR blocks are cast from CGI, and Ford uses it in some applications like the 2.7-liter EcoBoost V-6. And CGI is the secret sauce in making the Mongoose live under the pressure of its own power production.

That’s power as in 555 hp and a staggering 1230 lb-ft pumping though a new Allison 10-speed automatic transmission. In one bound, Chevrolet goes to the top of the class for torque. The 6.7-liter Cummins straight-six offered in Ram trucks peaks at 1075 lb-ft, and Ford’s 6.7-liter PowerStroke turbodiesel V-8 rates at 1200 lb-ft. Those numbers are absurd, and not far off those for a modern semi-truck tractor unit.

There is so much towing capacity that it’s hard to imagine how a civilian would use it all. How big must a cabin cruiser be to approach that much weight? And with so much torque, why head to the mountains when you could just pull them down? Yet the Mongoose-powered 3500 is a totally civilized monster that hauls out past the bounds of mortal experience.

A switch to electrically assisted rack-and-pinion steering for the HD, replacing the old steering box system, means a lightness to driver inputs that was previously missing. There was even some communication back through the wheel to my fingers. An electric brake booster also helps ensure that pedal pressure doesn’t need to be extreme to be effective.

As one engineer explained, the new Silverado is essentially a new truck below the cab. The high-end models on hand do ride astonishingly well even when unladen, which has often been the bugaboo of three-quarter-ton and one-ton pickups that are used to run errands when they’re not towing a three-story, five-bedroom Colonial to a new foundation.

If the Mongoose is overkill, the standard V-8 is a version of the new 6.6-liter small-block rated at 412 hp and 472 lb-ft. Running that engine in a properly configured truck drops the tow rating to a mere 19,000 pounds. Will that be enough?

The new Silverados are significantly better trucks than the 2026 editions. The attraction of so much naturally aspirated V-8 power makes the 1500 series compelling. It will be more than enough truck for most buyers. But for those who do want to haul more, or to brag about their ability to do so, the HD and the Mongoose engine provides this with utter civility. Diesel fuel is expensive, and adding emissions fluid is a pain, but it’s impossible not to like this much too much. I want one anyhow.

Long road trips hauling equipment for work or toys for play will be the ultimate test for both of these trucks. And those are tests that will be relished.

Pricing will be competitive with other full-size pickups because this is the meatiest part of the American new-vehicle market. It’s easy to reach $70,000 with a 1500 even without stretching to the ZR2. And a Silverado HD equipped with the big diesel and several layers of luxury gizmology will easily push beyond six figures. Americans love pickup trucks, and here’s more proof that pickup trucks are what American manufacturers do best.

#4504. Volkswagen’s new electric SUV is taking over where the ID.4 left off

Volkswagen is turning one of its best-selling nameplates into an electric SUV. The new ID. Tiguan is now rolling off the assembly line and will replace the ID.4 in 2027.

The ID.4 and ID.5 are on the way out, and the new ID. Tiguan will replace them in Volkswagen’s EV lineup next year.

Following the ID. Polo and ID. Cross, which are now on sale in Europe, the ID. Tiguan is the next model to go on sale as a “True Volkswagen,” as the company calls it.

The new electric SUV adopts Volkswagen’s best-selling nameplate, the Tiguan, as part of its shift away from the numerical system used on the outgoing ID.4 and ID.5.

Volkswagen announced on Thursday that series production of the electric ID. Tiguan has now begun at its Embden Plant in Germany.

“The Tiguan is our best-selling model worldwide, and the ID.4 and ID.5 are among our most successful electric cars,” VW Brand CEO Thomas Shafer said last month after unveiling the new SUV. He added that “The ID. Tiguan brings these two success stories together.”

The ID. Tiguan will be a step change from its predecessors, the ID.4 and ID.5, featuring Volkswagen’s “Pure Positive” design language, which includes an overhauled interior and exterior design and updated tech.

Volkswagen said the ID. Tiguan’s “hallmark feature” is the completely redesigned exterior. The new design remains closer to the gas-powered Tiguan, with a boxy, traditional SUV look.

Unlike the ID.4’s aerodynamic design, the new ID. Tiguan features a wide, chunky front end and traditional pull-style door handles instead of the flush ones.

In Volkswagen’s words, the new ID. Tiguan electric SUV “looks like a vehicle from the premium segment.”

Inside, the updates are just as evident. The overhauled interior features Volkswagen’s new infotainment setup, including a 10″ Digital Cockpit and a 15″ center display. There’s also an optional 12″ passenger screen available.

Another highlight is the return of physical buttons. After listening to customer feedback from current drivers, Volkswagen added physical buttons under the center display and on the steering wheel for climate control and other vehicle functions.

To spark a bit of nostalgia, VW added a fun new Retro Mode feature that transforms the Digital Cockpit and center display to mimic the style of iconic models like the first-generation Golf.

Drivers can also choose from six classic VW models to display in a virtual “garage” on the infotainment screen: Golf I, Golf II Country, Golf IV, Tiguan I, Race Touareg, and Beetle.

The new Volkswagen ID. Tiguan will be available with two battery packs and three performance levels:

Depending on the configuration, the ID. Tiguan offers a “new benchmark” for Volkswagen’s electric SUVs in Europe with a WLTP range of up to 377 miles (607 km).

Volkswagen opened orders for the ID. Tiguan in Germany and a few other European markets in October, starting at €42,695 ($47,800). It’s available in three trims: Trend, Life, and Style.

After it launches in Europe through early 2027, Volkswagen said the ID. Tiguan will go on sale in North America to replace the ID.4.

Apparently, the new ID Tiguan has a slightly better Cx (Drag Coefficient) at 0.26 versus 0.28 on first gen ID4 and 0.27 on 2nd gen. According to VW, it’s achieved using front air curtains, a minimal air intake, an enclosed underbody, and a longer roof spoiler.

Volkswagen said prices and other details will come in “due course.” The current VW ID.4 uses an 82 kWh battery that provides an EPA-estimated range of up to 291 miles in the RWD version. The AWD model offers around 263 miles.

Since the European model offers close to 25 miles (40 km) more WLTP range than the outgoing ID.4, the ID. Tiguan is expected to offer over 300 miles on the EPA scale.

Official US prices have not yet been announced. The outgoing ID.4 has a starting MSRP of about $45,000, so the ID. Tiguan will likely be priced similarly.

#4502. BYD’s new 5-seat luxury SUV brings big screens, big range, and starts at about $40,000

BYD launched the Denza N8 EV in China, a five-seat luxury SUV that promises more than 1,000 km (621 miles) of CLTC range, a tech-filled cabin, and plenty of premium extras.

Another day, another new BYD vehicle is now on sale in China. After opening preorders for the Denza N8 EV a few weeks ago, BYD held the grand launch event on Thursday.

The new N8 EV, or “the king of large 5-seater pure electric vehicles,” as Denza called it, is available in six variants, including four battery-electric (EV) and two plug-in hybrid (PHEV) powertrain options.

The all-electric Denza N8 starts at 269,900 yuan, or about $40,500, with prices ranging up to 329,900 yuan ($49,500) for the Flagship model. The PHEV models start at 300,900 yuan and 32,900 yuan, respectively.

Measuring 5,150 mm long, 1,999 mm wide, and 1,820 mm high, with a 3,075 mm wheelbase, the Denza N8 EV is slightly longer than the Kia EV9 and Hyundai IONIQ 9.

Inside, the interior is pretty over the top with a huge 30″ panoramic infotainment screen that stretches nearly the entire passenger-side dashboard. There’s also a new 43″ (1.1 meter) panoramic head-up display (PHUD) at the bottom of the windshield.

BYD added a few premium extras like front and rear zero-gravity seats, a drop-down ceiling entertainment screen, ambient lighting, and wireless phone chargers.

The Denza N8 is offered with a single rear-wheel-drive (RWD) or a tri-motor all-wheel-drive (AWD) powertrain. The RWD variant uses a single motor that delivers either 320 kW (429 hp) or 370 kW (496 hp), depending on the configuration.

The tri-motor Denza N8 debuts BYD’s e3 Evo technology. The setup includes three electric motors: a 270 kW (362 hp) front motor and two 310 kW (416 hp) rear motors, for a combined output of 890 kW (1,193 hp).

BYD’s Denza said the N8 EV boasts an all-electric CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles), “making it the world’s longest-range mass-produced all-electric SUV.”

To put it in perspective, that’s as much as the outgoing N8 plug-in hybrid (PHEV) it’s replacing, which offered a combined CLTC range of 1,003 km (623 miles) on a full tank of gas and a full charge.

It’s available with two second-gen BYD Blade battery packs: 105.792 kWh and 130.15 kWh, delivering CLTC ranges of up to 885 km (549 miles) and 1,003 km (623 miles).

With BYD’s second-gen Blade Batteries and Flash Charging tech, the Denza N8 EV can charge from 10% to 70% in five minutes. Charging from 10% to 97% takes just nine minutes.

Like many of its new luxury vehicles, the Denza N8 is equipped with BYD’s premium tech and features, such as its DiSus-A intelligent air suspension system and God’s Eye 5.0 intelligent driving assistance system.

BYD also sells the extended Denza N8L in China, which went on sale earlier this year, starting at 299,800 yuan ($45,000).

#4501. ‘GTA VI’ Is Going to Be Huge. Here’s the Gaming Gear You Need to Make the Most of It

Our car experts choose every product we feature. We may earn money from the links on this page.

After more than a decade of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally arriving on November 19. Here’s the gaming gear worth adding to your setup before launch day.

There are big video game releases, and then there’s Grand Theft Auto VI. After more than a decade, Rockstar’s next open-world blockbuster arrives November 19. Set in the fictional state of Leonida, with Vice City at its center, GTA VI is shaping up to be one of the biggest entertainment launches in history.

Rockstar has spent more than eight years developing the game, and while the exact development budget remains under wraps, outside estimates have put the investment somewhere around $1 billion to $1.5 billion. That’s a staggering figure, even by Hollywood standards. For perspective, its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, has sold more than 230 million copies, and outside estimates put its lifetime revenue above $10 billion.

Before GTA VI arrives, we’ve compiled a selection of the latest and greatest sim racing gear to make sure you’re ready for what promises to be the sim gaming event of the decade.

There are two editions of GTA VI available: the Standard Edition, which includes the base game, and the Ultimate Edition, which adds a collection of in-game extras, including vehicles, weapons, clothing, properties, and customization options. Ultimate Edition content is also available as a separate upgrade for Standard Edition owners, so you don’t have to make that decision at checkout.

Digital preloading is already underway on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, meaning players who have preordered can download the game ahead of launch and be ready to play on day one. Just make sure you have enough storage space.

With launch day approaching, now is a good time to take stock of your gaming setup. A quality headset, a comfortable controller, a responsive display, and the right accessories can make long sessions in Vice City that much better.

Order now from Amazon, and you’ll likely be in pole position by November 19.

#4499. KTM Reveals a New X-Bow Side-by-Side with a 330-HP Audi Engine

The new SXS balances a rowdy turbo four with a light chassis and capable suspension for endless Baja adventures.

About 20 years ago, KTM—an Austrian manufacturer best known in the United States for its motorcycles—broke into the sports car business with the KTM X-Bow. Now, the KTM X-Bow brand is doing some expanding of its own with a new premium side-by-side powered by an Audi engine and priced at up to nearly $100K.

KTM’s sports cars have historically used engines from the Volkswagen Group, and the new Arrow off-roader doesn’t break the mold. An Audi-sourced EA888 2.0-liter turbo four pairs with a seven-speed DSG transmission. The standard engine makes 280 horsepower, but the higher-priced Arrow Black Limited Edition is good for 330 horses. The EA888 is also used in the Audi A3 and S3, along with the GTI and R versions of the Volkswagen Golf. The X-Bow’s horsepower rating also beats the 2027 Polaris RZR Pro R, which tops out at 275 horses. That’s a pretty rowdy setup in the world of side-by-sides.

See all results for used KTM for sale near 72956

Front and rear limited-slip differentials, along with a chromoly steel chassis, help both Arrow variations fit right into Dakar-worthy off-road expeditions. A suspension with unequal-length control arms and dampers developed with KW Reiger allows for about 23.6 inches of travel.

Inside, both versions get Sabelt seats and harnesses. The standard Arrow variant features an open chassis, while the Black Limited Edition adds an enclosed cabin and air conditioning for even more comfort, as well as a fly-off handbrake for extra fun.

But air conditioning, race-inspired handbrakes, and 50 extra horses come at a cost. The Arrow Black Limited Edition will be limited to just 500 units, and it’ll only be available through a reservation process, which opens on November 17. The Black Limited Edition runs just under six figures with a starting price of $98,600.

After the Black Limited Edition goes on sale, the standard Arrow models will hit the market at $59,800. Sure, you could buy a brand new GTI, Golf R, S3, or A3 for less money, but they certainly couldn’t go where the Arrow could. KTM X-Bow says first deliveries are expected to start in late 2027.

#4497. Kia is giving the EV5 an update, and leaked images show what’s next

Kia isn’t wasting any time updating its Sportage-sized EV5 electric SUV. Leaked images just gave us our first look at what’s changing.

While Kia doesn’t sell the EV5 in the US, the electric SUV has been a hit in other global markets. It first went on sale in China in 2023, and Kia launched the global model last year; it is now available in Europe, Canada, the UK, and other overseas regions.

The electric SUV has played a major part in Kia’s turnaround in China and is among the top-selling EVs in places like Australia.

Kia is already preparing to introduce an updated version in 2027. The updated EV5 was revealed through Australian Design Rule (ADR) regulatory documents, including images of the new version and some powertrain specs.

Front- and all-wheel-drive variants will get a power boost with up to 234 hp (175 kW) in FWD and 334 hp (249 kW) for AWD models.

The new EV5 will still use the same 64.2 kWh and 88.1 kWh battery packs, but updated range figures have yet to be announced.

Kia’s current model offers a WLTP range of up to 248 miles (400 km) from the smaller battery and 345 miles (555 km) from the larger battery.

As previous spy images have shown, the updated Kia EV5 features a few slight exterior design changes.

These changes include new front and rear bumpers, similar to those of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

A post shared by SHORTS CAR (@shorts_car)

Saying there are updates with no context is borderline useless. A power boost from what? The EV5 isn't in the US, so I don't have its looks anywhere close to memorized.

Hopefully the power increase is more than just a software update, having hardware updates for better efficiency/lower weight/lower costs even if they're not passed on to consumers. If they're updating the looks, they should coincide with better aerodynamics for better higher speed range and efficiency.

Recent spy photos in Korea from ShortsCar revealed the EV5 update features a 27″ center infotainment screen, similar to the Hyundai Elexio and Kia Seltos that are made in China.

A sticker on the back said the vehicle was destined for the Philippines, meaning it’s the EV5 that’s produced in China.

Since Kia launched the China-made EV5 in 2023, it’s due for a refresh around 2027. Whether and when Kia will introduce the updated global version, which is produced in Korea, has yet to be confirmed.

#4496. Ford Expedition Tremor: Project Overland Asks What If?

You can’t buy one—at least not yet—but Ford designed it to match what real customers might want out of an overlanding Expedition.

You’ve probably already noticed, but off-road-ready vehicles are everywhere these days. Ford knows this all too well. It told Car and Driver that nearly 25 percent of its U.S. sales are off-road models, which is exactly why the automaker is looking to push the envelope a bit. Enter the Ford Expedition Tremor: Project Overland, Ford’s idea of how its customers would build an overlanding rig based on the rugged Expedition Tremor.

The Expedition Tremor: Project Overland was built as a one-off in collaboration between Fox Factory Vehicles and, according to the build sheet, the FoMoCo parts department. It rides on Fox dampers, of course, which give the Expedition a two-inch lift. The wheels come from the F-150 Raptor R, as do the chunky BFGoodrich KO2 all-terrain tires. The stock front bumper has been replaced with a modular F-150 Tremor bumper, complete with the Raptor’s hidden winch mount and a Warn winch.

See all results for new 2027 Ford Expedition / Expedition Max for sale near 21014

Lighting is handled via ditch, roof, and DC scene lights from Rigid, while a set of Tred Pro recovery boards is included to help with traction if this rig gets stuck. Once you’ve used all that gear to reach your campsite, the Yakima Skyrise HD Rooftop Tent, OverNOut awning, and Ford Liftgate side curtains will make the space more comfortable.

Ford described the project as a test bed for future possibilities and said that Fox and Ford viewed the build as insight into what customers might want from “purpose-built” full-size SUVs.

Since Ford and Fox Factory Vehicles built the Project Overland as an idea generator, you currently can’t actually order one from your local dealer. You can, of course, buy most of the parts for the build from their respective companies. Plus, if there’s enough interest, Ford could eventually put a more serious Expedition into production.

#4495. The Sanrivatti One Supercar Has an 800-HP Judd V-10 and a Motorcycle-Like Seating Position

If you were looking for something different from the norm ... this Dutch supercar sure does different.

There’s a new supercar company out of the Netherlands that, apparently, thinks the orientation we typically sit in to drive is out of style. It asks, what if your head was forward of your legs? And, what if you were kneeling as opposed to sitting? Strange, yes—but now such a machine exists. The car in question is called the Sanrivatti One, and the Dutch startup just revealed all the details.

The seating position, which you can check out below, is but one of the unique selling points (or disqualifying features) of the Sanrivatti One. All of the bits around the driver seem more likely to please folks. It has a mid-mounted 5.5-liter naturally aspirated Judd V-10 that makes 800 horsepower and 516 pound-feet of torque, and peak horsepower is produced at a beautiful 9000 rpm. There’s no electrification to be found, and all the power goes to the rear wheels via a Hewland six-speed sequential transmission.

The chassis consists of a carbon fiber monocoque, while a double-wishbone pushrod suspension keeps the 2425-pound car in balance. (Mind you, that quoted weight is dry weight, so expect the final curb weight to be higher.) Braking is handled by AP Racing carbon discs with six-piston calipers in both front and rear. Sanrivatti fits Michelin slick tires from the factory, making it a track-only affair. Said tires wrap 18-inch forged magnesium alloy wheels.

Acceleration figures aren’t available, but the Dutch company claims a 205-mph top speed. Its funky design and aero helps that effort, as Sanrivatti says the exterior is inspired by both the peregrine falcon and a fighter jet. The falcon can be seen in the single sweeping character line that seems to mimic a falcon’s wing in a dive; meanwhile, the single-piece canopy and nose-positioned intakes aim to evoke the aircraft. There’s a large wing that rises up and out from the diffuser, and the majority of the rear is otherwise left open to help dissipate heat from that big V-10.

Meanwhile, here’s what the company has to say about that wild driving position. “Creating an exceptional hypercar is difficult enough,” says Paul Arkesden, executive director of technology partnerships at Sanrivatti. “Creating one around an entirely different driving position means rethinking the relationship between packaging, structure, aerodynamics, ergonomics and controls from the outset. That is what makes the One so interesting.”

The final form of this seating position is similar to what you might experience on a motorcycle, so those who ride could find some familiarity there. Sanrivatti claims it offers about 3.2x better visibility than competitor supercars and track cars. And in case you were worried about being deeply uncomfortable (we sure are), Sanrivatti says it’s developing “proprietary body-support and control technologies” that “allow the driver to move more naturally with the vehicle while remaining supported and secured.”

While today marks the full public debut of the One, it’s still deep in testing stages, with track testing and prototype builds to come. There’s no target date for delivery as of now, so we’ll just need to wait and see what comes our way from Sanrivatti.
